data.name: Ysolina
data.gender_notes: Ysolina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word ‘ysoline’, which comes from the Greek word ‘ysos’, meaning ‘healing’ or ‘curing’. The name Ysolina is a variation of the name Isola, which means ‘island’, and it carries the same meaning of being a place of refuge and healing. The name Ysolina carries the meaning “God's healing” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ysolina usually hope their child will grow to embody god's healing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of hope and divine intervention, representing God's presence and healing power.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ysolina total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: יסולינה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יסולינה נגזר מהמילה העברית 'ישוע' שפירושה 'אלוהים הוא השומר' או 'אלוהים מציל', ומוסיף לסוף המילה את הסיומת הנשית 'ינה', שפירושה 'היא שומרת' או 'היא מצילה'. השם יסולינה משמש כהתייחסות לנוכחות האלוהית בחייה של הנושאת אותו.

in_greek.name: Ἰσολίνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ ὄνομα Ἰσολίνη προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑβραϊκὴ λέξη 'ישוע' (Yeshua), ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει 'Θεός ἐστι ὁ σωτήρ' ἢ 'Θεὸς ὁ φυλάσσων'. Ἡ προσθήκη τῆς θηλυκῆς κατάληξης '-ίνη' δηλώνει 'αὐτή ἡ φυλάσσωσα' ἢ 'αὐτή ἡ σωζομένη'. Ἰσολίνη ἐκφράζει τὴν παρουσίαν Θεοῦ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτῆς.

in_latin.name: Ysolina
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ysolina derivatur a voce hebraica 'ישוע' (Yeshua), quae significat 'Deus est salvator' vel 'Deus custodit'. Additio suffixi feminini '-ina' indicat 'illa quae custodit' vel 'illa quae salvatur'. Ysolina exprimit praesentiam divinam in vita sua.

Historically, the name reflects the biblical concept of God as a guardian and savior. Spiritually, Ysolina represents faith, security, and redemption.
